SUBJECT: SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENTS TO FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2022-
2023, 2023-2024, & 2024-2025 ANNUAL ACTION PLANS FOR THE COMMUNITY
DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS.

PURPOSE: To consider the proposed Substantial Amendments to the FY 2019-2020, 2020-2021,
2022-2023, 2023-2024, & 2024-2025 Annual Action Plans to reprogram $1,706,245 in CDBG funds.

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS: It is recommended that the Citizen Advisory Committee consider
staff's recommendation to reprogram CDBG funds and recommend to the City Council approval of
the proposed Substantial Amendments to the FY 2019-2020, 2020-2021, 2022-2023, 2023-2024, &
2024-2025 Annual Action Plans to reprogram $1,706,245 in CDBG funds.

ANALYSIS: Per HUD regulations, the City is required to carry out its Community Development
Block Grant (CDBG) program in a timely manner. As required by 24 CFR 570.902 of the CDBG
regulations, HUD reviews the City for compliance with these requirements each May 2. As part of a
detailed plan to correct course, staff propose reprogramming $1,706,245 of unused CDBG funds from
various Annual Action Plans to a construction-ready Street Improvement Project located in eligible
CDBG census tracts and consolidate all Commercial Fa9ade and Business Sign Programs funds into
one Commercial Fa9ade Program.

The Street Improvement Project will encompass street improvements within CDBG eligible census
tract areas:

  •  Industrial Avenue from Main Street to Century Boulevard.
  •  Frontage Road from Southern Avenue to Miller Way
  •  Pinehurst Avenue from Tweedy Boulevard to Southern A venue
  •  Hildreth Avenue from Southern Avenue to Tweedy Boulevard

Staff recommend allocating the available CDBG funds as follows:

BACKGROUND:  The City  of South  Gate has been a recipient  of CDBG  funds  annually  since the
enactment  of the Housing  and Community  Development  Act  of 1974.  The City  is deemed  as an

demographic  criteria.  CDBG  funding  can be used for a variety  of projects  and programs  primarily
benefiting  persons  of low-  and moderate-income.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The U.S. Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  ("HUD")  has not yet
announced  allocations  for local jurisdictions.  It is anticipated  that the City  of South Gate ("City")  will
receive  approximately  $6.2 million  in CDBG  entitlement  'funds,  and approximately  $2.8 million  in
HOME  entitlement  funds,  from  HUD  for FY 2025-2029.  The CDBG  and HOME  activities  and some
administrative  costs will  be funded  solely  by grant funds and will  not impact  the General  Fund.

ANALYSIS:  The  Five-year  Consolidated  Plan  (CONPLAN)  is a HUD  required  plan  assessing
affordable  housing  and community  development  needs for the next  five-year  2025-2029  period.  The
CONPLAN  determines  how  funds received  from  HUD  will  be used.

 BACKGROUND:  The City  of South  Gate is considered  an entitlement  jurisdiction  and receives  an
annual  allocation  from  the U.S.  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  (HUD)  for  the
operations  of its CDBG  and HOME  programs.  The funding  is determined  by a formula  calculated  by
HUD  based on population,  age of the city, poverty  levels,  etc. The City's  allocation  can fluctuate  year-
to-year  causing  funding  to increase  or decrease  in various  programs.

As a recipient  of the federal  funds,  the City  is required  to submit  a five-year  Consolidated  Plan,  an
Annual  Action  Plan,  and monitor  its progress,  outcomes,  and expenditures  through  the Consolidated
Annual  Performance  and Evaluation  Report  ("CAPER").

The purpose  of the CONPLAN  is to identify  the City's  housing  and community  development  needs,
priorities,  goals,  and strategies  and to stipulate  how funds will  be allocated  to housing  and community
development  activities  over the next  five  (5) years.  The CDBG  Program  provides  Federal  funds  for
local improvement  projects  and programs.  Activities  assisted  with  CDBG  funds must meet one of the
three (3) national  objectives:

  Benefit  low and moderate-income  persons;  or
  Aid  in the elimination  of slum and blight;  or
  Meet  a particular  urgent  community  need because  existing  conditions  pose a serious
  threat,  and no other  source  of funds  is available.  This  national  objective  is rare and is
  designated  only  for  activities  that  alleviate  emergency  conditions,  e.g.,  fire,  flood,
  earthquake.

The HOME  program  provides  formula  grants,  often in partnership  with  local nonprofit  groups,  to fund
a wide  range  of activities  including  building,  buying,  and/or  rehabilitating  affordable  housing  or
providing  direct  rental  assistance  to low-income  persons.  HOME  is the largest  Federal  Block  Grant to
State  and Local  Governrnents  designed  exclusively  to create  affordable  housing  for  low-income
households.

NEXT  STEPS  IN  THE  PROCESS:  HUD  requires  two public  hearings  during  the development  of
the Consolidated  Plan.  The  first  public  hearing  was conducted  during  the City  Council's  regular
meeting  on Tuesday,  February  11, 2025.  The purpose  of this hearing  was to gather  input  from  the
community  regarding  their  needs and to discuss  potential  goals for consideration  in the development
of  the  five-year  Consolidated  Plan.  Following  the  public  input,  we  will  prepare  drafts  of  the
Consolidated  Plans  and Annual  Action  Plan.  Once these drafts  are completed,  they will  be finalized
for review.  The City  is required  to conduct  a 30-day  comment  period  and hold a second public  hearing
to adopt the five-year  Consolidated  Plan and additional  reports.  FY  2025/2026  Annual  Action  Plan
